title: Build the preview host list from the environment with an agent-team preview-hosts command
acceptance: New src/ui/hosts.ts exports parseHostList(value) (split on commas, trim, lower-case, drop empty values and duplicates) and previewHosts(env): the union, in order, of parseHostList(env.AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS), the host name of each set and valid URL in APP_URL, PUBLIC_URL, BASE_URL, ORIGIN, NEXTAUTH_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, and env.HOSTNAME when it is a valid host name. Names are lower-cased, with no port, no empty entries, and no duplicates. No host name is hard-coded.
src/ui/server.ts uses parseHostList for its extra hosts in place of the inline split, with the same behavior. allowedHost, allowedOrigin, knownHost, and the auth checks do not change.
New CLI subcommand `agent-team preview-hosts` in src/cli.ts prints previewHosts(process.env).join(",") and nothing else, and is listed in the usage text.

The deploy.json start command sets AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS="$(node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning src/cli.ts preview-hosts)" in place of the node -p one-liner. The hash step, the ui command, install, and port stay the same.

test/hosts.test.ts covers: empty env gives []; AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS=" a.example, ,A.example" gives ["a.example"]; APP_URL=http://agent-team-qa-agent-team:4400 gives ["agent-team-qa-agent-team"]; HOSTNAME=agent-team-qa-agent-team with no APP_URL gives the same; APP_URL="not a url" and HOSTNAME="" are skipped; all set with overlaps gives each name once.
test/deploy-start.test.ts is updated to the new start command: it runs the host-list part in sh offline and checks the list for example environments.

test/preview-host.test.ts starts the server with AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS=previewHosts({ HOSTNAME: "agent-team-qa-agent-team" }).join(",") and a password hash: GET on /, /login, /new, /import, /incidents, and /settings with Host: agent-team-qa-agent-team:4400 answers 200, and GET / with Host: evil.example answers 403 with "This host name is not allowed. Add it to AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS." The shell body check is skipped when web/dist is missing.

New test/hash-password.test.ts runs `node src/cli.ts hash-password` with execFileSync, stdin set to a 12+ character password with no trailing newline, and checks the login password check from src/ui/auth.ts accepts exactly that password and rejects it with a trailing space. It runs offline.
The login form, sessions, and lockouts do not change.
verify: npm run typecheck && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test test/hosts.test.ts test/deploy-start.test.ts test/preview-host.test.ts test/hash-password.test.ts test/auth.test.ts test/dashboard.test.ts

title: Add config for GitHub issue polling and the Codex base URL
acceptance: loadConfig reads publish.github.issues.enabled (default true) and publish.github.issues.everyMinutes (default 10). everyMinutes outside 1 to 1440 fails with a plain message.
loadConfig reads an optional runners.codex block with baseUrl and apiKeyEnv, exposed on the config as runners.codex ({ baseUrl, apiKeyEnv } or null when unset).
A baseUrl that does not parse as an http: or https: URL (for example ftp://x or "not a url") fails with "Set codex base URL to a full http or https URL."
apiKeyEnv must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ (the same rule as operate.posthog.apiKeyEnv), so "sk-123 abc" fails with a plain message. apiKeyEnv without baseUrl fails with a plain message.
A pipeline.yaml with neither block still loads as before.
pipeline.example.yaml shows both blocks, commented, with apiKeyEnv as an env var name and never a key.
test/config.test.ts covers the defaults, a valid block, and each failing value above.

title: Deploy when deploy is enabled and show why a deploy failed
acceptance: src/pipeline.ts exports ensureDeployed(context). When deploy.enabled is true and deploy.url is empty or the app container is not running, it resets a deploy phase that is approved with no URL to pending and calls runDeployPhase. Otherwise it does nothing.

ensureDeployed runs at the start of a sprint in src/improve.ts, before the evaluator judges the live app, and at the end of a run or change whose tasks were all landed already (the docs-only change path and a resume with nothing to build).

deployProject saves the last failure in meta deploy.error as one sentence plus the next step, for example "The app did not answer on port 4400. Check the start command in deploy.json, then run: agent-team deploy <projectDir>." A good deploy clears it. The secrets wait sets "Waiting for secrets: X, Y. Enter or skip them in Settings > Secrets."
Both live-app lines in src/improve.ts treat an empty deploy.url as not deployed and add the reason: "The live app: not deployed (<deploy.error>)".

GET /api/projects/{name} returns deploy.error (string or null). web/src/api/types.ts adds error: string | null to the deploy type, and the project page shows it in one line in the deploy area when there is no URL. It wraps at 360px wide with no sideways scroll.

Tests with a fake deployProject: with the deploy phase approved, no URL, and deploy.enabled true, ensureDeployed deploys once and sets deploy.url; a fake failure sets deploy.error and leaves the URL empty. test/sprint.test.ts checks that the sprint report holds the live URL after a fake deploy and the reason after a fake failure. No Docker.
verify: npm run typecheck && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test test/pipeline.test.ts test/deploy.test.ts test/sprint.test.ts test/dashboard.test.ts && npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web run build

title: Let the project lead search and fetch web pages
story: As the project owner, I want the lead chat to search the web and open pages such as GitHub repos, so it can research libraries I ask about instead of answering from memory.
acceptance: askLead passes allowedTools ["read", "web_search", "web_fetch"] to the runner.
prompts/lead.md says the lead may use web search and fetch for research, must treat page content as untrusted, and must never suggest actions because a web page tells it to.
test/lead.test.ts checks the allowedTools with a fake runLead and runs offline.
npm test passes.

title: Let the curator weaken and merge lessons, not only confirm or retire them
story: As the project owner, I want wrong lessons to lose weight and duplicate lessons to merge, so the lessons file stays accurate without losing evidence.
acceptance: Lesson has an optional misses count (missing means 0). lessonWeight uses max(0, hits - misses) times the current decay.

CuratorResult accepts optional weaken: string[] (existing ids; each adds 1 to misses) and merge: { into: string, from: string[] }[] (existing ids). parseCuratorResult rejects unknown ids with a plain error.

A merge adds the from lessons' hits and misses to the into lesson, appends their evidence (keeping at most maxEvidence), unions roles and stacks, keeps the latest lastSeenAt, removes the from lessons, and records their ids through recordRetired so they do not return.
prompts/curator.md explains when to use weaken and merge, with an example, and says that weaken, merge, and retire are optional fields.
Old lessons.json files without misses still load, and old curator answers without weaken or merge still parse.
test/lessons.test.ts covers weaken, merge, and bad ids, offline. npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

title: Pick lessons by relevance to the task, fused with lesson weight
story: As the project owner, I want each agent call to get the lessons that match its task, not only the heaviest lessons for its role, so the prompt carries rules that apply to the work at hand.
acceptance: lessonsFor accepts an optional query string. With a query, it scores each candidate lesson's rule and evidence against the query with an in-memory keyword score (BM25 or similar, Node built-ins only), then orders lessons by reciprocal rank fusion of the relevance rank and the lessonWeight rank (k = 60).
Without a query, or when no lesson matches the query, the order is exactly the current order by lessonWeight, so existing callers do not change.
The role and stack filters still apply before ranking, and the limit still applies after ranking.
withLessons in src/pipeline.ts passes the task prompt as the query; if ranking throws, the agent call still runs without lessons, as today.
test/lessons.test.ts covers relevance winning over a slightly heavier unrelated lesson, the no-query fallback, and the stack filter, offline.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

title: Create missing GitHub labels on existing repositories
story: As the project owner, I want imported repositories to get the agent-team labels, so task issues are created instead of failing on every run.
acceptance: When the repository already has an origin, the orchestrator creates the labels from the labels list with `gh label create --force` once per project, and records a store meta flag so it does not repeat on every run.
Label creation stays best effort: a failure is logged through attempt() and the run continues.
createIssue retries without labels if gh fails because a label is missing, so the issue is still created and its number is stored.
test/github.test.ts covers label creation for an existing origin and the no-label fallback, offline, with a fake gh on PATH. npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

title: Always allow the APP_URL host in the preview start command
story: As the project owner, I want the preview to accept its public APP_URL host even when AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS is already set, so opening the preview does not answer 403.
acceptance: The start command in deploy.json appends the APP_URL host name to any existing AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS value (comma-separated) instead of using it only as a fallback. It still works when AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS is empty or APP_URL is unset, and never produces a leading or trailing comma.

test/deploy-start.test.ts runs the host-list part of the deploy.json start command in a shell with AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS=other.example and APP_URL=https://app.example and checks that both hosts are in the result; it also covers the empty and unset cases. Offline, no Docker.
docs/architecture.md says that the APP_URL host is added to AGENT_TEAM_UI_HOSTS, not only used as a default.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

title: Let the project lead run with full access when lead.access is full
story: As the project owner, I want to let the chat lead edit files and run any command in the project, so it can fix things and deploy without a separate task.
acceptance: pipeline.yaml accepts lead.access with the value "read" (the default) or "full", next to the existing lead.actions and lead.autoApply keys. loadConfig reads it, and config validation rejects any other value with a plain error message.
With lead.access read, askLead passes allowedTools ["read", "web_search", "web_fetch"] exactly as before.
With lead.access full, askLead also passes edit, write and an unrestricted bash tool, and sets no writablePaths, so the lead can edit any file in the project folder and run any command there.
toClaudeTools maps a plain "bash" tool to the unrestricted Claude "Bash" tool. The existing "bash:<prefix>" rules still map as before.

In full mode, prompts/lead.md tells the lead that it may edit files and run commands, that it works directly on the project's main checkout without review, and that it must list every file it changed and every command it ran in its reply. In read mode, the prompt keeps the current text that says the lead cannot edit or run commands.
test/lead.test.ts covers both modes with a fake runLead and checks the allowedTools and the system prompt. Tests run offline and call no real agent.
docs/architecture.md documents lead.access, its default, and the risk that full mode skips the worktree, reviewer and PR.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

title: Fail a QA round when no page renders
acceptance: src/qa.ts exports noPageRenderedMessage = "No page rendered. Check the host and start command." and noPageRendered(visual). It returns false when visual is null; true when visual.startError is set, visual.routes is empty, or every route failed. A route failed when it has an error, a null status, a 403 or 5xx status, or no screenshot file. One route with a 2xx or 3xx status and a screenshot makes it false.

In the QA round in src/pipeline.ts, after splitFailures, noPageRenderedMessage is pushed onto hardFailures when noPageRendered(visual) is true, so it can never be filed as preexisting, and a "pass" verdict is rejected. The round logs `round N: No page rendered. Check the host and start command.`
splitFailures and createBaseline do not change.

test/qa.test.ts covers: every route 403 gives true; every route with status null and an error gives true; startError with no routes gives true; one route 200 with a file and the rest 403 gives false; visual null gives false.

title: Add autonomy.decide: auto so the run never waits for a human
story: As the project owner, I want the run to make the best decision on its own instead of stopping at requireHuman, so the project stays autonomous. Add `autonomy.decide: human | auto` to pipeline.yaml (default `human`). With `auto`, every place that calls requireHuman decides by itself and logs why: scope blocks approve the requested files without the maxAutoApprovals limit, but if the task asks again for files it already has, mark it blocked, open a GitHub issue for the record, and continue with other tasks; a task out of budget gets +50% once if the run budget allows, otherwise it is skipped; a doctor edit that needed a human is applied directly. The run-wide spend limit still applies. Also turn it on for this project by setting `decide: auto` under `autonomy` in pipeline.yaml.
acceptance: loadConfig reads autonomy.decide as 'human' or 'auto', defaults to 'human', and throws a plain error for any other value.

With decide: auto, a scope block is approved without the maxAutoApprovals limit, unless the task asks for files it already has; then the task is marked blocked, an issue is opened, and the run continues with other tasks without awaiting_approval.
With decide: auto, a task that runs out of its per-task budget gets +50% once when the run budget allows it; otherwise it is skipped and the run continues.
With decide: auto, a doctor edit that required a human is applied directly.
Every automatic decision logs a line with the reason, using the existing event log.
With decide: human (the default), behavior is unchanged.
This project's pipeline.yaml has `decide: auto` under `autonomy`.
docs/architecture.md documents autonomy.decide and its risks.
Tests cover each decision path offline with fakes.

title: Make the lead chat full screen and responsive on phones
story: On a phone (360-412px wide) the Build > Chat screen breaks. Follow-up chips in FollowUps (chat-tab.tsx) overflow to the right and cause a horizontal scrollbar, because the Button base class has whitespace-nowrap and shrink-0 and the chips have no max width. The Thread height is calc(100dvh-11rem), but the page header (breadcrumb, title, status badges) takes about a third of the screen, so the page scrolls and the chat sits in a small card. The composer textarea is fixed at 2 rows and squeezed by the image, mic, and send buttons, so the placeholder is cut off. Make the chat feel like a messaging app on phones: full screen and fluid.
acceptance: At 360px and 412px wide, the chat page has no horizontal scroll: follow-up chips, action cards, code blocks, and long paths stay within the screen (chips wrap or scroll sideways in their own row).

Below the sm breakpoint, the chat fills the space below the app top bar edge to edge: no card border or side margin, the page heading and breadcrumb are hidden or collapsed to one compact line, and the composer stays pinned at the bottom above the safe area, including when the mobile keyboard is open (use dvh).

The composer textarea starts at one line and grows with the text up to about 40% of the viewport. The placeholder is short enough to fit on phones. Image and mic buttons stay tappable (at least 36px) without squeezing the textarea.
The message list keeps scrolled to the newest message as new messages or live activity arrive, unless the person scrolled up; then a 'Jump to latest' button appears.
Message bubbles on phones use almost the full width (the avatar may be hidden or smaller), and the desktop layout (sm and up, xl with the context card) keeps working as before.
npm --prefix web run lint and npm --prefix web run build pass.
verify: npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web run build && npm run typecheck

title: Stop merges into main from failing on local changes
story: As an operator, I want a change or task merge into main to work even when the main checkout has uncommitted edits, so the run does not stop and the doctor does not burn its attempts on the same error.
acceptance: Before merging, mergeIntoMain checks git status in the project folder.
If tracked files are dirty, it stashes them with a named message such as 'agent-team: auto-stash before merging <branch>', merges, and logs '[merge] stashed local changes: <files>'.
If the merge fails, it aborts the merge and restores the stash, so the folder is left as it was, then throws a plain error that names the files.
Untracked files that the merge does not touch do not block the merge.

test/workspace.test.ts covers: a clean main, a dirty main (the merge works and the stash exists), and a merge conflict (the stash is restored). It uses temp git repos and sets user.name and user.email.

title: Make the doctor escalate early when the same stop repeats
story: As an operator, I want the doctor to hand an incident to me as soon as it repeats a fix that did not work, so it does not spend all its attempts and budget on the same stop.
acceptance: Each doctor attempt records a fix signature on the incident: the diagnosed cause, the sorted list of project actions, and whether it landed a code fix.

When the same stop comes back after a fix that had no code fix (only a resume or project actions), incidentFor gives up at once with the reason 'the same stop came back and the last fix changed no code', and it does not start a new attempt.
When the same stop comes back and the last fix signature matches an earlier attempt on the same incident, the doctor gives up at once with a reason that says the fix repeated.

On an early give-up, the doctor opens a 'Decision needed' notice (or comments on the incident issue) that lists the earlier attempts and their actions, and logs '[doctor] incident <id>: escalated early: <reason>'.
Other incidents still use maxAttempts and maxUsdPerIncident as before.

test/doctor.test.ts covers: a stop that repeats after a resume-only fix (escalates with no new attempt), a stop that repeats with the same signature (escalates), and a stop that repeats after a different code fix (tries again). It uses temp folders and fakes and does not call agents or GitHub.

title: Select backlog items and start building them as one change
story: As the project owner, I want to tick the backlog items I approve and start building them in one step, so I do not have to approve them one by one or wait for the next sprint.
acceptance: src/operate/findings.ts exports approveFindings(projectDir, store, ids) that checks every id first (404 for an unknown id, 409 for an item that is not open, 400 for an empty list or more than 20 ids) and then opens one change through openChange.

The change request lists each item's title and proposal, then a 'Backlog items:' trail with '- #<id> [<source>, <severity>] <title>'. The request stays within changeRequestMaxLength and trims the item text, not the trail.

After the change opens, every picked item has status 'approved' and the change id, and the store logs '[operate] findings <ids> approved as change <id>'. If openChange throws (a run is alive, a change is open, the build is not done), no item changes status.

POST /api/projects/:name/findings/approve with { ids: number[] } answers 201 { changeId, branch, started } and starts the run like the single-item route. It answers 409 when a run is alive and { error } with a 4xx status for bad input. The existing single-item route still works.
In Operate > Backlog, each open item row has a checkbox with an accessible label. Ticking it does not open the detail panel; clicking the row still does. Dismissed items have no checkbox.

When one or more items are ticked, a bar shows 'N selected' with 'Start development' and 'Clear'. 'Start development' calls the new route, shows a toast with the change id, clears the selection, and refreshes the list. It is disabled while a run is active, with the same note the detail panel shows.
The layout works at 360px wide: the bar stays visible (sticky at the bottom on mobile) and the checkboxes are at least 44px tap targets.
api.approveFindings is added to web/src/api/client.ts, the route is added to contracts/openapi.yaml, and docs/sprints.md explains that you can start picked items without waiting for a sprint.

test/operate.test.ts covers: several ids open one change and approve all of them; an unknown or dismissed id rejects the call and changes nothing; openChange refusing leaves all items open; and the HTTP route returns 201 and 409. The tests use temp folders and fakes.
verify: npm run typecheck && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test test/operate.test.ts && npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web run build

title: Remove the old run container and wait for it before resuming
acceptance: startRunContainer in src/project.ts takes injectable deps ({ docker, processAlive, sleep }) with real defaults, and is exported (or calls an exported replaceRunContainer(name, deps)). runContainerArgs does not change.
Before docker run it calls docker inspect on the run's container name. When inspect fails, it goes straight to docker run.
When the container exists and the store's run.pid is alive, it throws "A run for this project is still going. Stop it before you resume." and calls neither rm nor run.

Otherwise it calls docker rm -f <name>, then polls docker inspect every 250 ms until it fails, for at most 30 seconds, and only then calls docker run. On timeout it throws "The old run container <name> did not go away. Remove it with: docker rm -f <name>".

test/run-container.test.ts has a fake docker that records calls: with a dead run and inspect finding the container for two polls, the order is inspect, rm -f, inspect (found), inspect (found), inspect (missing), run. A second case with a live run throws and records no rm and no run. No real Docker, and sleep is faked.

title: Make sprints and routines run on this project and report what blocks them
acceptance: agent-team sprint <projectDir> --check and agent-team routines <projectDir> --check print the blocker from sprintBlocker and from routineBlocker for each routine in plain words (or "ready"), and exit 0.
buildComplete in src/project.ts accepts an imported project whose phases the importer marked approved.
syncSprint closes a change stuck in open with no live run as failed, with a reason, so it no longer blocks sprints.

When the operator starts a sprint or runs a routine and it is blocked, the API answers 409 { "error": "<blocker>" }, and the Sprints and Routines screens show that error in a toast. No path returns quietly.

test/sprint.test.ts: from an imported-project fixture with approved findings and deploy.enabled true, sprintBlocker returns null, and a sprint run with fake runners and a fake deploy creates a sprint row that ends in a final state (done or failed), never planning.
test/routines.test.ts: runRoutine for monitoring with a fake runner records lastRun and adds its findings; a routine with output: sprint adds a sprint row.
Tests use temp folders and fakes, and call no agents or Docker.
verify: npm run typecheck && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test test/sprint.test.ts test/routines.test.ts test/dashboard.test.ts test/run-container.test.ts && npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web run build

title: Publish the Docker image to ghcr.io on each release
acceptance: .github/workflows/release-image.yml runs on release types [published], with permissions contents: read and packages: write.

Its steps use actions/checkout@v4, docker/setup-qemu-action@v3, docker/setup-buildx-action@v3, docker/login-action@v3 to ghcr.io with github.actor and secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, docker/metadata-action@v5 for ghcr.io/vinicius3333/agent-team with tags type=raw,value=${{ github.event.release.tag_name }} and type=raw,value=latest, and docker/build-push-action@v6 with context ., file Dockerfile, push true, platforms linux/amd64,linux/arm64. It runs no tests and uses no other secret.

title: Poll GitHub issues labeled agent-team into the backlog
acceptance: src/operate/issues.ts exports issueFingerprint(repo, number) returning github-issue:<owner>/<repo>#<number>, syncIssues({ projectDir, store, config, gh, appUrl, now }) with gh an injected (args) => string, and issuesTick({ runsDir, now }).

syncIssues skips a project when publish.github.enabled is false, publish.github.issues.enabled is false, or the project has no GitHub repo. Otherwise it runs gh issue list --repo <owner>/<repo> --label agent-team --state open --json number,title,body,url --limit 100.

Each issue with no finding for its fingerprint becomes one open finding through the existing backlog or findings insert: source github, severity medium, title cut to backlogTitleMaxLength, evidence the issue URL, proposal the body cut to 8,000 characters.

After the finding exists and meta github.issue.<number>.commented is unset, it runs gh issue comment once with "agent-team added this issue to the backlog of <project> as item #<id>: <link>", then sets the meta. The link is <APP_URL without trailing slash> plus the real backlog route with #finding-<id>; with no APP_URL the text ends at "item #<id>." with no link.
It logs "[issues] <project>: added N, commented N". A gh failure logs one line and skips that project until the next poll.
issuesTick polls each project whose meta github.issues.polledAt is older than publish.github.issues.everyMinutes. The long-lived doctor loop calls it next to sprintTick; --once does not poll.
Each backlog item in Operate > Backlog renders id="finding-<id>" so the comment link lands on it.

test/issues.test.ts with a fake gh and a temp store: two issues give two findings with the right title, evidence, and fingerprint, and two comments with the link from appUrl; a second sync adds and comments nothing; a comment that throws once leads to exactly one comment on the next sync; no appUrl gives a comment with no URL; publish.github.enabled false makes no gh call.
verify: npm run typecheck && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test test/issues.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts && npm --prefix web run lint && npm --prefix web run build

title: Let the Codex runner use an OpenAI-compatible base URL
acceptance: RunRequest gains codex?: { baseUrl: string; apiKeyEnv: string | null }, filled from config.runners.codex wherever a RunRequest is built (harness, lead, operate agents, routines).

With baseUrl set, the Codex runner adds -c model_provider="agent-team" and -c model_providers.agent-team={ name = "agent-team", base_url = "<baseUrl>", env_key = "<apiKeyEnv>", wire_api = "chat" }. The key value never goes in the args. Without baseUrl the args are the same as today.
When apiKeyEnv is named but unset in the environment, the run fails before the agent starts with "Set <NAME> in the environment for the codex base URL."
In the Docker sandbox a Codex run with apiKeyEnv passes a bare -e <NAME>, like CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. The network allowlist adds the baseUrl host and port for the run.

test/runners.test.ts with a fake executor: with baseUrl and apiKeyEnv the args hold the provider config with that URL and env name, and neither the args, the transcript, nor the events hold the key value; without baseUrl the args equal today's. test/harness.test.ts or test/network.test.ts checks the bare -e flag and the allowed host. Offline, no real agents or Docker.
verify: npm run typecheck && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test test/runners.test.ts test/harness.test.ts test/network.test.ts test/routines.test.ts
